title: Puy lentil salad with radishes, orange and watercress

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain staple: lentils, seeds, oranges, radishes, herbs, Dijon mustard and olive oil.

supermarket.reason: Puy lentils, watercress, pumpkin seeds and the rest are on everyday Tesco shelves at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, sieve, bowl, whisk and knife, and cutting the peel off an orange is within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 250g dry lentils in a litre of water feeds four at lunch, and dressing them while warm with seasoned oil and orange juice gives a well-flavoured salad, though a splash of vinegar would sharpen it.

honest_times.reason: Toasting the seeds, slicing the onion and radishes, peeling two oranges and chopping parsley fits in about 20 minutes, and the 35-minute total is close to the simmer plus resting time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm lentil salad with 200g of radishes and a good bunch of watercress suits a mid-April lunch, and the radishes are a main part rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, ordered sensibly and written in plain British English without fuss.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils and seeds bring protein and fibre with plenty of fresh veg and fruit, so it makes a filling lunch rather than a side salad.
